newsitem.title: USA: Chubb life unit attracting interest.
newsitem.headline: Chubb life unit attracting interest.

text.p: Chubb Corp said a number of potential purchasers have expressed an interest in buying its life insurance business, which the company put up for sale late last year.

Chubb chief executive Dean O'Hare said an evaluation of strategic options last year indicated that a sale of the life insurance business was likely to yield the greatest immediate value for Chubb shareholders.
O'Hare said its 1996 preliminary results do not reflect any financial impact of a potential sale since the impact of such a sale is not yet known.
Chubb in October said it had retained Goldman Sachs & Co to assist it in evaluating its strategic options for the life insurance companies.
In December, Chubb said it had decided to pursue a sale of the business.
Chubb also in October said it was considering a possible sale of some or all of the properties of its Bellemead Development Corp subsidiary.
O'Hare said Chubb is currently reviewing a number of alternatives regarding its real estate business.

Chubb expects to receive proposals from parties interested in purchasing a substantial portion of its portfolio of office buildings and will consider its next steps in light of these proposals, O'Hare said.
A report in Barron's in January said Chubb was considering offering its real estate business to the public through an initial public offering.
